1→# Bivvy Development Workflow
     2→
     3→> Atomic development workflow for building Bivvy.
     4→
     5→<steps>
     6→  <step number="1" id="specification">
     7→    <title>Specification</title>
     8→    <goal>Define the contract your code must fulfill before writing implementation.</goal>
     9→    <instructions>
    10→      <instruction>
    11→        Define the Behavior: Create test files first. Tests are the specification.
    12→        <conditional>
    13→          <condition>Test files already exist</condition>
    14→          <action>Update tests to match the new/changed behavior</action>
    15→        </conditional>
    16→      </instruction>
    17→      <instruction>
    18→        <command>cargo test --all-features</command>
    19→        <expected>All new or updated tests should FAIL</expected>
    20→        <rationale>Failing tests prove they're actually testing new logic, not passing by accident.</rationale>
    21→      </instruction>
    22→    </instructions>
    23→    <gate>
    24→      <condition>New tests fail for the right reasons</condition>
    25→      <on_fail>Refine your tests until they correctly specify the behavior</on_fail>
    26→    </gate>
    27→  </step>
    28→
    29→  <step number="2" id="implementation">
    30→    <title>Implementation</title>
    31→    <goal>Write the minimum code to make tests pass.</goal>
    32→    <prerequisite ref="specification">Failing tests from specification step</prerequisite>
    33→    <instructions>
    34→      <instruction>
    35→        Write the Code: Implement only what's needed to pass the tests. Resist adding "nice to have" features.
    36→      </instruction>
    37→      <instruction>
    38→        Keep it Simple: If you're writing more code than tests require, stop and reconsider.
    39→      </instruction>
    40→    </instructions>
    41→    <gate>
    42→      <condition>All tests pass</condition>
    43→      <on_fail>Continue implementing or fix bugs until green</on_fail>
    44→    </gate>
    45→  </step>
    46→
    47→  <step number="3" id="documentation">
    48→    <title>Documentation</title>
    49→    <goal>Document while context is fresh. User-facing and dev-facing docs are separate concerns.</goal>
    50→    <prerequisite ref="implementation">Tests passing</prerequisite>
    51→    <instructions>
    52→      <instruction>
    53→        Rustdoc Comments: Add `///` doc comments to all public items (structs, functions, modules). This is the primary form of API documentation.
    54→      </instruction>
    55→      <instruction>
    56→        User-Facing Docs: Update `docs/` if adding commands, config options, or user-visible features. These are Starlight pages written for end users — never reference internals.
    57→      </instruction>
    58→      <instruction>
    59→        Source READMEs: Update or create `README.md` in source directories (e.g., `src/cli/README.md`) when adding or changing subsystem design, architecture, or guiding principles.
    60→      </instruction>
    61→      <instruction>
    62→        Inline Comments: Add comments only where the "why" isn't obvious from the code.
    63→      </instruction>
    64→      <instruction>
    65→        Verify Docs Build: Confirm documentation compiles without errors.
    66→        <command>cargo doc --no-deps --all-features</command>
    67→        <expected>No documentation errors</expected>
    68→      </instruction>
    69→    </instructions>
    70→    <boundaries>
    71→      <rule>Developer docs go in source tree (rustdoc + source READMEs), never in `docs/`</rule>
    72→      <rule>User-facing docs go in `docs/`, never in source READMEs</rule>
    73→    </boundaries>
    74→    <anti-patterns>
    75→      <anti-pattern>Documenting "what" the code does (the code should show that)</anti-pattern>
    76→      <anti-pattern>Leaving documentation for later (it won't happen)</anti-pattern>
    77→      <anti-pattern>Over-commenting obvious code</anti-pattern>
    78→      <anti-pattern>Putting developer architecture docs in `docs/`</anti-pattern>
    79→      <anti-pattern>Putting user-facing guides in source READMEs</anti-pattern>
    80→    </anti-patterns>
    81→  </step>
    82→
    83→  <step number="4" id="linting">
    84→    <title>Static Quality Gate (Linting)</title>
    85→    <goal>Catch issues before they become problems.</goal>
    86→    <prerequisite ref="documentation">Implementation and documentation complete</prerequisite>
    87→    <instructions>
    88→      <instruction>
    89→        <command>cargo fmt -- --check</command>
    90→        <expected>No formatting differences</expected>
    91→        <fix>cargo fmt</fix>
    92→      </instruction>
    93→      <instruction>
    94→        <command>cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings</command>
    95→        <expected>No warnings or errors</expected>
    96→        <rationale>Warnings today become bugs tomorrow. Zero tolerance. Flags match CI.</rationale>
    97→      </instruction>
    98→    </instructions>
    99→    <gate>
   100→      <condition>Both commands pass with zero output</condition>
   101→      <on_fail goto="implementation">Fix all issues. Return to implementation if code changes are needed.</on_fail>
   102→    </gate>
   103→  </step>
   104→
   105→  <step number="5" id="testing">
   106→    <title>Verification Gate (Full Test Suite)</title>
   107→    <goal>Ensure nothing is broken.</goal>
   108→    <prerequisite ref="linting">Linting passes</prerequisite>
   109→    <critical>
   110→      ALWAYS run `cargo test --all-features` without filters. NEVER use:
   111→      - cargo test some_name
   112→      - cargo test module::
   113→      - cargo test --lib
   114→      The ENTIRE test suite must pass with all features. "X filtered out" means you ran it wrong.
   115→      The --all-features flag matches CI - skipping it locally may cause CI failures.
   116→    </critical>
   117→    <instructions>
   118→      <instruction>
   119→        <command>cargo test --all-features</command>
   120→        <expected>All tests pass (new and existing), 0 filtered out</expected>
   121→      </instruction>
   122→      <instruction>
   123→        <command>cargo llvm-cov --all-features --fail-under-lines 90</command>
   124→        <expected>Coverage at or above 90%</expected>
   125→        <conditional>
   126→          <condition>cargo-llvm-cov not installed</condition>
   127→          <action>Skip coverage check locally; CI will enforce</action>
   128→        </conditional>
   129→      </instruction>
   130→    </instructions>
   131→    <gate>
   132→      <condition>All tests pass, coverage threshold met</condition>
   133→      <on_fail goto="implementation">Do not proceed with failing tests.</on_fail>
   134→    </gate>
   135→  </step>
   136→
   137→  <step number="6" id="build">
   138→    <title>Integration Gate (Build Verification)</title>
   139→    <goal>Confirm production readiness.</goal>
   140→    <prerequisite ref="testing">All tests passing</prerequisite>
   141→    <instructions>
   142→      <instruction>
   143→        <command>cargo build --all-targets --all-features</command>
   144→        <expected>Build succeeds with no warnings</expected>
   145→        <rationale>RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" in CI means any warning fails the build. Flags match CI.</rationale>
   146→      </instruction>
   147→      <instruction>
   148→        <command>cargo build --release</command>
   149→        <expected>Release build succeeds</expected>
   150→        <rationale>Catches release-only issues (optimizations, LTO problems).</rationale>
   151→      </instruction>
   152→    </instructions>
   153→    <gate>
   154→      <condition>Both builds succeed silently</condition>
   155→      <on_fail goto="linting">Treat warnings as errors. Return to linting or implementation until clean.</on_fail>
   156→    </gate>
   157→  </step>
   158→
   159→  <step number="7" id="commit">
   160→    <title>The Atomic Commit</title>
   161→    <goal>Create a single, complete unit of work.</goal>
   162→    <prerequisite ref="build">All gates passed (lint, test, build)</prerequisite>
   163→    <instructions>
   164→      <instruction>
   165→        Stage Selectively: Add only the files related to this change.
   166→        <command>git add [specific files]</command>
   167→        <anti-pattern>git add -A (may include unrelated changes)</anti-pattern>
   168→      </instruction>
   169→      <instruction>
   170→        Write the Message: Explain WHY, not just WHAT.
   171→        <format>
   172→          <line>Short description in imperative mood, 50 chars or less</line>
   173→          <line></line>
   174→          <line>Longer explanation of why this change was made,</line>
   175→          <line>what problem it solves, and any important context.</line>
   176→          <line>Wrap at 72 characters.</line>
   177→        </format>
   178→        <rules>
   179→          <rule>Imperative mood ("Add feature" not "Added feature")</rule>
   180→          <rule>Capitalize first letter, no period at end</rule>
   181→          <rule>No type prefixes (no "feat:", "fix:", etc.)</rule>
   182→        </rules>
   183→      </instruction>
   184→      <instruction>
   185→        Verify Atomicity: This commit should be independently checkable, buildable, testable, and documented.
   186→      </instruction>
   187→    </instructions>
   188→    <gate>
   189→      <condition>Commit contains code + tests + docs for one logical change</condition>
   190→      <on_fail>Split into smaller commits or add missing pieces</on_fail>
   191→    </gate>
   192→  </step>
   193→
   194→  <step number="8" id="post-commit">
   195→    <title>Post-Commit Verification</title>
   196→    <goal>Confirm the commit didn't break anything.</goal>
   197→    <prerequisite ref="commit">Commit created</prerequisite>
   198→    <instructions>
   199→      <instruction>
   200→        <command>cargo test</command>
   201→        <expected>Still passing after commit</expected>
   202→      </instruction>
   203→      <instruction>
   204→        <command>cargo build</command>
   205→        <expected>Build succeeds with no warnings</expected>
   206→      </instruction>
   207→      <instruction>
   208→        <command>git log -1 --stat</command>
   209→        <rationale>Review what was actually committed</rationale>
   210→      </instruction>
   211→    </instructions>
   212→  </step>
   213→
   214→  <step number="9" id="transition">
   215→    <title>Transition</title>
   216→    <goal>Clean context switch to next task.</goal>
   217→    <instructions>
   218→      <instruction>
   219→        Clean Slate: Clear your mental context. The previous task is done.
   220→      </instruction>
   221→      <instruction goto="specification">
   222→        Next Task: Pick the next item from your backlog and return to specification.
   223→      </instruction>
   224→    </instructions>
   225→  </step>
   226→</steps>

   228→<verification-commands>
   229→  <description>Quick reference for all verification commands in order (matches CI):</description>
   230→  <command-sequence>
   231→    <command>cargo doc --no-deps --all-features</command>
   232→    <command>cargo fmt -- --check</command>
   233→    <command>cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings</command>
   234→    <command note="NO FILTERS - run entire suite with all features">cargo test --all-features</command>
   235→    <command>cargo build --all-targets --all-features</command>
   236→    <command>cargo build --release</command>
   237→    <command>cargo llvm-cov --all-features --fail-under-lines 90</command>
   238→  </command-sequence>
   239→  <critical>
   240→    `cargo test --all-features` must be run WITHOUT name filters. Never filter tests.
   241→    Output must show "0 filtered out" - any other number is wrong.
   242→    All flags (--all-targets, --all-features) match CI exactly.
   243→  </critical>
   244→</verification-commands>
   245→
   246→<principles>
   247→  <principle name="Atomic">Each commit is complete and independent</principle>
   248→  <principle name="Test-First">Tests define behavior before implementation</principle>
   249→  <principle name="Zero-Warning">Warnings are errors; fix them immediately</principle>
   250→  <principle name="Document-As-You-Go">Docs are part of the deliverable, not an afterthought</principle>
   251→  <principle name="Small-Steps">Prefer many small commits over few large ones</principle>
   252→</principles>

## Comprehensive Analysis of Bivvy Configuration Loading Mechanism

Based on my thorough exploration of the Bivvy codebase, here's a complete breakdown of the configuration system:

---

### **1. CONFIG FILE LOADING MECHANISM**

**File Locations and Discovery** (`src/config/loader.rs`):
- **Project config**: `.bivvy/config.yml` (required to exist for a valid project)
- **Local overrides**: `.bivvy/config.local.yml` (gitignored, optional)
- **User global config**: `~/.bivvy/config.yml` (system-wide, optional)
- **Remote extends**: URLs specified in `extends:` field (optional)

**Discovery Order** (via `ConfigPaths::discover()`):
1. Check for `.bivvy` directory presence (primary indicator of project root)
2. Fallback to `.git` directory if no `.bivvy` found
3. Walk up directory tree until found

**Loading Priority** (later overrides earlier):
1. Remote base configs (from `extends:` URLs)
2. User global config (`~/.bivvy/config.yml`)
3. Project config (`.bivvy/config.yml`)
4. Local overrides (`.bivvy/config.local.yml`)

---

### **2. CONFIG DATA STRUCTURES**

**Root Structure** (`BivvyConfig` in `schema.rs`):
```rust
pub struct BivvyConfig {
    pub app_name: Option<String>,
    pub settings: Settings,
    pub template_sources: Vec<TemplateSource>,
    pub steps: HashMap<String, StepConfig>,
    pub workflows: HashMap<String, WorkflowConfig>,
    pub secrets: HashMap<String, SecretConfig>,
    pub extends: Option<Vec<ExtendsConfig>>,
    pub requirements: HashMap<String, CustomRequirement>,
    pub vars: HashMap<String, VarDefinition>,
}
```

**Key Sub-structures**:
- **`Settings`**: Global defaults (output mode, logging, parallel execution, environments)
- **`StepConfig`**: Individual step definitions with 20+ fields (command, template, depends_on, completed_check, prompts, env overrides, etc.)
- **`WorkflowConfig`**: Named workflow definitions with step lists and step-specific overrides
- **`CompletedCheck`**: Idempotency detection (file_exists, command_succeeds, marker, all/any combinations)
- **`PromptConfig`**: Interactive prompts (select, multiselect, confirm, input)
- **`VarDefinition`**: Variables - either static strings or computed from shell commands
- **`ExtendsConfig`**: Remote config inheritance (just URL field)

---

### **3. YAML HANDLING AND PARSING**

**serde_yaml vs marked-yaml**:
- **`serde_yaml`** (version 0.9): Used for ALL config loading and parsing
  - Parses YAML into `serde_yaml::Value` for merging
  - Then deserializes to `BivvyConfig` struct
  - See `loader.rs` lines 162-166: `serde_yaml::from_str(content)`
  - And lines 172-187: `load_config_value()` returns raw `serde_yaml::Value`

- **`marked-yaml`** (version 0.8.0): Planned but NOT currently used for config
  - Comment in `lint.rs` line 149: "Would need actual byte offsets from marked_yaml"
  - Currently a dependency listed in `Cargo.toml` but not integrated into config loading
  - Intended future use: source location tracking for lint error reporting

---

### **4. MERGE/LAYERING LOGIC**

**Deep Merge Algorithm** (`src/config/merger.rs`):

```rust
pub fn deep_merge(base: &Value, overlay: &Value) -> Value
pub fn merge_configs(configs: &[Value]) -> Value
```

**Merge Rules**:
1. **Objects (maps)**: Merged recursively
2. **Arrays**: Completely replaced (not appended)
3. **Null values in overlay**: Delete the corresponding key from base
4. **Scalars**: Overlay value replaces base value
5. **Leaf keys special case**: The `environments` key has special handling
   - Maps are merged (entries added/replaced)
   - But each entry VALUE replaces entirely instead of recursing

**Example Merge Behavior**:
```yaml
# Base
settings:
  output: verbose
  logging: true
steps:
  database:
    command: "rails db:setup"
    watches: [schema.rb]

# Overlay
settings:
  output: quiet
steps:
  database:
    command: "rails db:prepare"

# Result
settings:
  output: quiet        # overridden
  logging: true        # preserved
steps:
  database:
    command: "rails db:prepare"  # overridden
    watches: [schema.rb]         # preserved
```

---

### **5. FILE LOADING FLOW**

**Main Entry Point**: `load_merged_config(project_root: &Path) -> Result<BivvyConfig>`

**Step-by-step process** (from `loader.rs` lines 201-246):

1. **Discover** config files via `ConfigPaths::discover(project_root)`
   - Sets `user_global`, `project`, `project_local` paths
   - Validates project config exists, else returns `ConfigNotFound` error

2. **Load as raw values** - all configs loaded as `serde_yaml::Value`:
   ```rust
   for path in paths.all_existing() {
       let value = load_config_value(path)?;  // Returns raw Value
       configs.push(value);
   }
   ```

3. **Merge** all values in order:
   ```rust
   let merged = merge_configs(&configs);
   ```

4. **Deserialize** merged value to `BivvyConfig`:
   ```rust
   let config: BivvyConfig = serde_yaml::from_value(merged)?;
   ```

5. **Resolve extends** if present:
   ```rust
   if config.extends.is_some() {
       let resolved = resolver.resolve(&config)?;
       return Ok(resolved);
   }
   ```

---

### **6. EXTENDS RESOLUTION**

**Remote Config Inheritance** (`src/config/extends.rs`):

**`ExtendsResolver` workflow**:
1. Fetch each remote config URL via `RemoteFetcher`
2. Parse remote config recursively (may itself have `extends:`)
3. Merge each resolved remote config into accumulator
4. Merge local config on top (local overrides remotes)
5. Clear `extends` field from final config (already resolved)
6. Convert back to `BivvyConfig`

**Cycle Detection**: Tracks visited URLs to prevent infinite loops

**Security**: SSRF prevention with blocked hosts list:
- `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `0.0.0.0`, `[::1]`
- Cloud metadata IPs: `169.254.169.254`, `100.100.100.200`

---

### **7. REMOTE FETCHING**

**`RemoteFetcher`** (`src/config/remote.rs`):
- Timeout: 30 seconds (configurable)
- Cache directory: `~/.cache/bivvy/remote-configs/`
- HTTP client: reqwest with blocking API and rustls
- Cache management: ETags and git-based strategies (planned)
- Authentication: Bearer tokens and custom headers supported

---

### **8. KEY REFERENCE POINTS IN CODEBASE**

**File Paths Referenced**:
- Line 48-54: `~/.bivvy/config.yml` - user global config
- Line 57-64: `.bivvy/config.yml` - project config
- Line 66-74: `.bivvy/config.local.yml` - local override

**Main Config Loading Functions** (exported from `mod.rs`):
- `load_config()` - with optional override
- `load_config_file()` - single file
- `load_config_value()` - raw Value
- `load_merged_config()` - full merge pipeline
- `load_merged_config_with_resolver()` - testable version
- `parse_config()` - string to struct

---

### **9. COMPREHENSIVE TESTING**

**Test Coverage** (`src/config/loader.rs` lines 261-704):
- Config discovery with/without user global
- Project root finding (.bivvy vs .git priority)
- Preference for .bivvy over .git
- File not found errors
- Parse error handling
- Empty file handling
- Full config parsing
- Merge precedence (local overrides project)
- Step preservation during merge
- Extended config resolution
- Merge order with extends
- Local override with extends
- Circular dependency detection

**Integration Tests** (`tests/config_api_test.rs`):
- Full workflow: load → validate → interpolate
- Config merge workflow
- Interpolation context with project/env

---

### **10. DEPENDENCY VERSIONS** (from `Cargo.toml`)

```toml
serde_yaml = "0.9"           # YAML parsing
marked-yaml = "0.8.0"        # Future: source tracking
serde = "1.0.228"            # Serialization
reqwest = "0.13.1"           # HTTP fetching
chrono = "0.4.43"            # Time handling
dirs = "6.0.0"               # Config dir discovery
```

---

### **SUMMARY**

The Bivvy configuration system is **layered, merge-based, and extensible**:

- **Discovery**: Walks up filesystem looking for `.bivvy` (or `.git`)
- **Loading**: Finds configs in 4 locations with clear precedence
- **Parsing**: Uses `serde_yaml` for all YAML → Rust conversions
- **Merging**: Deep recursive merge with special handling for arrays and leaf keys
- **Extension**: Remote base configs via `extends:` with SSRF protection
- **Merging**: `marked-yaml` is a dependency but not yet integrated (planned for lint improvements)
- **Validation**: Post-merge structural validation ensuring steps/workflows reference exist
- **Testing**: Extensive unit and integration tests covering all paths

The system allows sophisticated configuration composition while maintaining simplicity - each layer overrides in a predictable way, with arrays being replaced entirely rather than merged.

The config loading lives in `src/config/loader.rs`. Key facts:

1. `load_config_value(path)` reads file as string, parses with `serde_yaml::from_str` → `serde_yaml::Value`

3. `serde_yaml::from_value(merged)` deserializes the merged value into `BivvyConfig`

### Schema
- `BivvyConfig` struct in `schema.rs` uses `#[derive(Deserialize)]` with serde — so it's format-agnostic already
- The merger operates on `serde_yaml::Value` which is the intermediate representation

### Dependencies (Cargo.toml)
- `serde_yaml = "0.9"` for YAML
- `serde = "1.0.228"` with derive
- `serde_json = "1.0.149"` (already present)
- No `toml` crate yet

### Init Command
- `src/cli/commands/init.rs` line 258: writes `.bivvy/config.yml` with YAML content
- Line 46: checks if `.bivvy/config.yml` exists

- About 60+ references to `config.yml` across the codebase
- Tests create `.bivvy/config.yml` files in tempdir

## Requirements
- Allow users to use `bivvy.toml` (or `.bivvy/config.toml`) instead of `.bivvy/config.yml`
- Parse TOML using the `toml` crate
- Both formats should work with the existing merge pipeline
- Should not break any existing YAML functionality

## Key Design Decision

The merger currently operates on `serde_yaml::Value`. For TOML support, we have a few options:

**Option A: Convert TOML → serde_yaml::Value**
- Parse TOML with `toml::from_str` into `toml::Value`, then convert to `serde_yaml::Value`
- Pro: Minimal changes to merger, all existing code works
- Con: Conversion step is slightly inelegant

**Option B: Use serde_json::Value as intermediate**
- Replace `serde_yaml::Value` with `serde_json::Value` everywhere in the merger
- Parse YAML → json::Value, TOML → json::Value, then merge
- Pro: More "neutral" intermediate format
- Con: Larger refactor, serde_yaml::Value handles YAML-specific features

**Option C: Convert via serde (serialize → deserialize)**
- Parse TOML to `toml::Value`, serialize to JSON string, deserialize as `serde_yaml::Value`
- Pro: Simple roundtrip
- Con: Inefficient

Recommend **Option A** — it's the least disruptive. The `toml::Value` and `serde_yaml::Value` types are structurally similar (both are enum-of-scalar-and-collection types). A small conversion function handles it.

1. Adding the `toml` dependency to Cargo.toml
2. Modifying `ConfigPaths` to discover `.toml` variants
3. Adding a format detection function (by extension)

9. What about user-global config — should `~/.bivvy/config.toml` also be supported?

Keep the plan focused and practical. Remember the project follows test-first development.

Users currently must write Bivvy config in YAML (`.bivvy/config.yml`). This change adds TOML as an alternative format (`.bivvy/config.toml`), parsed with the `toml` crate. Both formats work with the existing merge pipeline. YAML remains the default.

## Approach

**Convert TOML → `serde_yaml::Value` before merging.** The merger operates on `serde_yaml::Value` and is well-tested. A small `toml_value_to_yaml_value` conversion function lets TOML configs enter the same pipeline with zero changes to the merger.

Precedence rule: **YAML wins over TOML** when both exist at the same location.

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `Cargo.toml` | Add `toml = "0.8"` |
| `src/config/loader.rs` | `ConfigFormat` enum, `toml_value_to_yaml_value()`, update `find_*` methods, `load_config_value`, `parse_config` |
| `src/config/mod.rs` | Export `ConfigFormat`, update module docs |
| `src/cli/commands/init.rs` | `config_exists()` checks for TOML too |
| `src/cli/args.rs` | Update `--config` help text |

**Unchanged:** `merger.rs`, `extends.rs`, `validator.rs`, `schema.rs`, all existing tests.

Add `toml = "0.8"` to `Cargo.toml` under `[dependencies]`.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ConfigFormat { Yaml, Toml }

impl ConfigFormat {
    pub fn from_path(path: &Path) -> Option<Self> {
        match path.extension().and_then(|e| e.to_str()) {
            Some("yml") | Some("yaml") => Some(Self::Yaml),
            Some("toml") => Some(Self::Toml),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}
```
Export from `mod.rs`. Tests: detect yml/yaml/toml, None for unknown/missing extension.

### 3. Add `toml_value_to_yaml_value` conversion (`loader.rs`)
Recursive function mapping `toml::Value` variants → `serde_yaml::Value`. Datetimes become strings. Tests: string, int, float, bool, array, nested table, datetime.

### 4. Update `ConfigPaths` discovery (`loader.rs`)
Each `find_*` method checks `.yml` first, then `.toml` as fallback:
- `find_user_global`: `~/.bivvy/config.yml` → `~/.bivvy/config.toml`
- `find_project_config`: `.bivvy/config.yml` → `.bivvy/config.toml`
- `find_project_local`: `.bivvy/config.local.yml` → `.bivvy/config.local.toml`

Tests: discovers TOML when no YAML exists, prefers YAML over TOML.

### 5. Update `load_config_value` for format detection (`loader.rs`)
Detect format via `ConfigFormat::from_path` (default: YAML). For TOML: parse with `toml::from_str` then convert via `toml_value_to_yaml_value`. Tests: loads TOML file, returns parse error for invalid TOML.

### 6. Update `parse_config` for format detection (`loader.rs`)
For TOML: use `toml::from_str::<BivvyConfig>` directly (serde is format-agnostic, no conversion needed for single-file parsing). Tests: parses TOML content, returns error for invalid TOML.

### 7. Fix hardcoded error path in `load_merged_config_with_resolver`
Line 235: use actual discovered project config path instead of hardcoded `config.yml`.

### 8. End-to-end tests
- TOML-only project config loads correctly
- TOML project + YAML local override merges correctly
- YAML project + TOML local override merges correctly

### 9. Update `init.rs`
- `config_exists()`: also check `.bivvy/config.toml`

### 10. Update help text
- `src/cli/args.rs` line 16: mention TOML alternative

### 11. Update doc comments
All `config.yml` references in `loader.rs` and `mod.rs` docs get TOML mentions.

- **No null in TOML**: The "null overlay deletes key" merge pattern can't be expressed in TOML. Users needing this must use YAML for that layer.

```bash
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo fmt -- --check
cargo build --all-targets --all-features
cargo build --release
```
